notes: This lesson is about how to think about money, not a calculation. There is nothing to act on or to check against a rule.

blocks.text: Money is a Tool. Not a Master.
PROTOCOL: HUMAN RESTORATION
True Wealth is 5-Dimensional
Most Indians optimize for only ONE dimension (Financial). The other 4 collapse, leading to a "Rich but Miserable" life.
🧠 Mental Wealth: Can you sleep without pills?
❤️ Emotional Wealth: Does anyone actually know you?
🕰️ Time Wealth: Do you own your morning?
🏃 Physical Wealth: Can you climb 4 floors?

blocks.label: What money can buy: VIP Care
What it cannot buy: The Will to Live
blocks.text: Money buys the ventilator, but it cannot buy the breath. It buys the bed, but not sleep. It buys the nurse, but not the hand of a loved one holding yours in the final moment.

blocks.label: The page's one-line summary
blocks.text: Wealth stops at the hospital reception.

blocks.label: What money can buy: The Grand Event
What it cannot buy: The Happy Marriage
blocks.text: Money buys the applause of relatives who won't even remember the food next week. It cannot buy the laughter in the bedroom, the patience during fights, or the loyalty in tough times.

blocks.label: The page's one-line summary
blocks.text: A wedding is a day. Marriage is a lifetime.

blocks.label: What money can buy: The Luxury 4BHK
What it cannot buy: The Home
blocks.text: Money buys the address. It cannot buy the warmth at the dinner table. A 4000 sqft house feels like a prison if the people inside it don't talk to each other.

blocks.label: The page's one-line summary
blocks.text: Peace does not require square footage.

blocks.label: What money can buy: The CEO Title
What it cannot buy: The Purpose
blocks.text: Money buys the envy of your peers. It cannot buy the feeling of meaning when you wake up. It cannot fix the anxiety of imposter syndrome or the loneliness at the top.

blocks.label: The page's one-line summary
blocks.text: Your resume is not your eulogy.

blocks.label: What money can buy: The 10 Crore Corpus
What it cannot buy: The Vitality
blocks.text: Money buys the ticket to Europe. It cannot buy the knees to walk the streets of Paris. It buys the best food, but not the digestion to enjoy it.

blocks.label: The page's one-line summary
blocks.text: Don't save joy for a time when you can't digest it.
The Hustle Begins
"Let me work hard now. I'll travel later." You skip family functions. You eat at your desk. You trade health for a promotion.
The Golden Handcuffs
You have the money now. But now you have EMIs. And kids. And stress. "Let me pay off the house, then I'll relax."
The Wake Up Call
Parents are gone. Kids are busy. Health gives the first warning shot (BP/Sugar). "I wish I spent more time when they were around."
Your accountant tracks money. Who tracks your soul?
ASSETS (Peace Sources) VALUE

"Log Kya Kahenge" Bankruptcy
The finish line moves every time you get close to it.
You ran faster. But the line moved further.
The Busy Executive
"I wish I hadn't worked so hard."
I missed my children's childhood for a promotion nobody remembers now.
The People Pleaser
"I wish I lived for myself."
I bought a big house to impress relatives who didn't even like me.
The Worrier
"I wish I let myself be happier."
I saved joy for 'later'. Later never came the way I imagined.
"If a decision gives you more money, but less peace, less connection, and less health... It is a bad trade."
